name: New Apostolic Reformation
scope: The New Apostolic Reformation (NAR) as C. Peter Wagner named and set it out: a charismatic Christian movement of independent church networks led by modern apostles and prophets (the restored fivefold ministry of Ephesians 4:11), whose dominion theology holds that the church is to take dominion over every sphere of society (the Seven Mountains of religion, family, education, government, media, arts and entertainment, and business) so that God's kingdom comes on earth, advanced by spiritual warfare. The defining sources are Wagner's own accounts (his essay on the NAR and dominion mandate, and his books Churchquake!, Apostles Today and Dominion!, as summarised by scholars), the scholarship on him and the movement (Resane, Woodfield, Budiselić), and secondary accounts (the Southern Poverty Law Center, Modern Reformation, and Wagner's former assistant writing in the Christian Post). Sources agree the NAR has no membership or creed, so the profile covers what those sources attribute to the movement's apostolic-prophetic networks and Wagner's teaching, not every independent charismatic church and not the political commitments of individual adherents or politicians linked to it. It excludes the New Apostolic Church (a separate denomination), Christian reconstructionism (a separate Reformed strand of dominionism), and the broader apostolic-prophetic movement beyond what these sources tie to the NAR name. Critics' claims (theocracy, fascism, Christian supremacy) are not taken as its own positions; Wagner himself rejects theocracy and 'ecclesiocracy'.

clerical-rule.rationale: Wagner states he rejects theocracy and 'even more so an imagined "ecclesiocracy" in which the church would rule'; the organised church stays in the Religion Mountain and civil government is a function of the Government Mountain.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Wagner cites Romans 13 approvingly: 'there is no authority except from God, and the authorities that exist are appointed by God', and grounds his programme in God's kingdom being done on earth.

more-religion-public.rationale: Wagner's dominion mandate calls on the church and kingdom-minded Christians to influence or 'take dominion' of all seven spheres of society (religion, family, education, media, government, arts, business), so that God's kingdom comes on earth.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Wagner's NAR teaching treats societal change as spiritual warfare against Satan and territorial demons: God's people must wage strategic warfare to retake authority from Satan, and the sources agree this is central to the movement.

separate-church-state.rationale: Wagner keeps the church as an organised body apart from civil government (the two 'should not be confused') yet wants believers to take the highest government offices to bring God's will to every sphere; the sources state both and do not address strict separation directly.

summary: The New Apostolic Reformation is a loose charismatic Christian movement, named by C. Peter Wagner, of independent church networks led by modern apostles and prophets. Its dominion theology holds that Christians should take dominion over every sphere of society (the Seven Mountains) so that God's kingdom comes on earth, advanced by spiritual warfare against demonic powers. Wagner himself rejects theocracy and church rule, and the sources record little on most concrete policy questions.
notes: Concrete policy positions are thin. Critics (SPLC) are not counted as the movement own positions.
